MUHAMMADIYAH.OR.ID, PALU – Presiden Republik Indonesia, Prabowo Subianto, mengajak Muhammadiyah untuk terus memperkuat kolaborasi dan kerja sama antarelemen bangsa dalam menjaga persatuan di tengah keberagaman Indonesia. Menurutnya, kebersamaan para pemimpin menjadi salah satu kunci keberhasilan sebuah bangsa.

Pesan tersebut disampaikan Presiden Republik Indonesia Prabowo Subianto saat memberikan sambutan dalam Pembukaan Tanwir dan Milad ke-114 Muhammadiyah di Gedung Banua Kaili (GBK) H. Rusdy Toana, Universitas Muhammadiyah Palu, Sulawesi Tengah, Sabtu (13/11).

Prabowo menilai, Indonesia sebagai negara majemuk membutuhkan kesadaran bersama untuk mengesampingkan kepentingan kelompok dan membangun kerja sama demi kepentingan bangsa.

“Bangsa yang berhasil adalah bangsa yang unsur pemimpinnya bisa bekerja sama,” tegas Prabowo.

Ia menuturkan, sejak awal pengabdiannya di dunia militer, keselamatan bangsa dan rakyat menjadi prinsip utama yang selalu dipegang. Dalam menjalankan tanggung jawab tersebut, diperlukan semangat gotong royong, suasana damai, serta kolaborasi antara seluruh elemen kepemimpinan.

Prabowo juga mengingatkan bahwa perbedaan latar belakang, suku, pandangan, dan organisasi merupakan kenyataan yang tidak dapat dipisahkan dari kehidupan bangsa Indonesia. Karena itu, setiap kelompok perlu memiliki kesadaran untuk hidup berdampingan dan bekerja sama, bukan memaksakan kehendaknya sendiri.

“Pilihan kita adalah apakah ingin memaksakan kehendak kelompok sendiri atau memiliki kesadaran untuk bekerja sama dengan semua kelompok lainnya,” ujarnya.

Dalam kesempatan tersebut, Prabowo turut menyampaikan apresiasi terhadap kiprah Muhammadiyah yang dinilainya telah memberikan kontribusi nyata bagi bangsa dan rakyat Indonesia melalui bidang pendidikan, kesehatan, serta berbagai pelayanan sosial.

Ia menilai, kekuatan Muhammadiyah terletak pada kesungguhannya dalam menjalankan pengabdian melalui karya nyata yang manfaatnya dapat dirasakan langsung oleh masyarakat.

“Kebesaran Muhammadiyah adalah karena Muhammadiyah bekerja sungguh-sungguh dan mengabdi secara nyata kepada bangsa dan rakyat Indonesia,” ungkapnya.

Prabowo kemudian memaparkan sejumlah capaian amal usaha Muhammadiyah, mulai dari 165 perguruan tinggi, 24 fakultas kedokteran, 130 rumah sakit, sekitar 8.000 sekolah dasar hingga menengah, serta 20.000 taman kanak-kanak.

Menurutnya, besarnya jaringan amal usaha tersebut menunjukkan kualitas kepemimpinan dan kemampuan manajemen organisasi Muhammadiyah dalam mengelola berbagai bidang pengabdian.

Ia juga menyoroti kuatnya tradisi pendidikan Muhammadiyah yang dinilai menjadi salah satu ciri utama persyarikatan dalam mencerdaskan kehidupan bangsa.

Melalui Tanwir dan Milad ke-114 Muhammadiyah, semangat kolaborasi dan persatuan tersebut menjadi pesan penting bagi seluruh elemen bangsa untuk terus bergotong royong, merawat keberagaman, dan membangun Indonesia.

Presiden Prabowo Ajak Muhammadiyah Perkuat Kolaborasi untuk Menjaga Persatuan Bangsa

MUHAMMADIYAH.OR.ID, PALU – Presiden Republik Indonesia, Prabowo Subianto, mengingatkan pentingnya menjadikan nilai Shiratal Mustaqim atau Jalan yang Lurus sebagai pedoman dalam kehidupan berbangsa dan bernegara. Menurutnya, bangsa Indonesia harus berani membedakan antara kebenaran dan kebatilan serta menjauhi keserakahan yang dapat merusak kehidupan masyarakat.

Pesan tersebut disampaikan Presiden Prabowo pada Sabtu (14/11) saat memberikan sambutan dalam Pembukaan Tanwir dan Milad ke-114 Muhammadiyah di Gedung Banua Kaili (GBK) H. Rusdy Toana, Universitas Muhammadiyah Palu, Kota Palu, Sulawesi Tengah.

Di hadapan pimpinan dan warga Muhammadiyah, Prabowo mengungkapkan bahwa ajaran Siratalmustaqim menjadi salah satu nilai yang terus terngiang dalam ingatannya sejak belajar dari para guru dan tokoh agama.

“Saya belajar dari guru-guru saya, kiai-kiai saya, ustaz-ustaz saya. Yang paling utama terngiang-ngiang di saya adalah Shiratal Mustaqim itu,” ungkap Prabowo.

Ia menjelaskan bahwa dalam kehidupan manusia selalu terdapat dua jalan yang berbeda, yakni jalan kebenaran dan jalan kebatilan. Ada kelompok yang memilih jalan lurus, tetapi ada pula yang terjebak dalam keserakahan dan kejahatan.

Prabowo kemudian mengaitkan nilai tersebut dengan persoalan pengelolaan kekayaan bangsa. Ia menyayangkan kekayaan Indonesia yang melimpah belum sepenuhnya dinikmati oleh rakyat karena masih adanya praktik penyalahgunaan kekuasaan dan kepentingan segelintir pihak.

Menurutnya, keserakahan dan praktik korupsi menjadi persoalan serius yang harus dihadapi melalui perbaikan sistem pengelolaan negara. Ia menegaskan bahwa kekayaan bangsa semestinya digunakan untuk meningkatkan kesejahteraan seluruh rakyat Indonesia.

“Yang kita kerjakan adalah bagaimana memperbaiki sistem yang keliru dan menyelamatkan kekayaan rakyat Indonesia supaya bisa dinikmati oleh seluruh rakyat Indonesia,” tegasnya.

Prabowo juga menekankan bahwa tujuan utama pembangunan nasional adalah menghapus kemiskinan dan kelaparan. Ia menilai tidak seharusnya negara yang memiliki kekayaan alam melimpah masih membiarkan masyarakatnya hidup dalam kesulitan.

“Tujuan kita adalah harus kita hilangkan kemiskinan dari bumi Indonesia dan harus kita hilangkan kelaparan dari bumi Indonesia,” ujarnya.

Lebih lanjut, Prabowo mengingatkan pentingnya menjaga demokrasi agar tidak dikuasai oleh kekuatan uang dan kepentingan kelompok tertentu. Ia juga mengajak seluruh elemen bangsa untuk tidak mudah terpecah belah oleh ambisi dan kepentingan sempit.

Dalam konteks perjuangan kebangsaan, Presiden Prabowo turut menyebut KH Ahmad Dahlan dan Ki Bagus Hadikusumo sebagai tokoh bangsa yang memiliki cita-cita besar bagi Indonesia. Ia meyakini perjuangan para pendiri bangsa tidak ditujukan untuk membangun negara yang membiarkan ketidakadilan dan kemiskinan terus berlangsung.

Melalui forum Tanwir dan Milad ke-114 Muhammadiyah, pesan tentang jalan yang lurus tersebut menjadi pengingat bahwa pengabdian kepada bangsa harus dilandasi nilai kebenaran, integritas, dan keberpihakan kepada kepentingan rakyat. (taufik)

Prabowo di Tanwir Muhammadiyah: Jalan Lurus Harus Jadi Pedoman dalam Kehidupan Berbangsa

MUHAMMADIYAH.OR.ID, YOGYAKARTA — Ketua Majelis Tarjih dan Tajdid Pimpinan Pusat Muhammadiyah Ustadi Hamsah mengajak umat Islam membangun kesadaran bahwa setiap aktivitas kehidupan memiliki keterhubungan dengan Allah Swt.

Kesadaran tersebut penting agar manusia tidak terjebak pada anggapan bahwa keberhasilan hidup semata-mata merupakan hasil kemampuan dan jerih payah dirinya sendiri.

Pesan tersebut disampaikan Ustadi dalam Pengajian Tarjih pada Rabu (11/11), ketika menjelaskan kandungan Surah Ali Imran ayat 28 tentang larangan menjadikan orang-orang kafir sebagai aulia atau sekutu dengan mengesampingkan orang-orang beriman.

Ustadi menjelaskan bahwa salah satu pesan penting dari ayat tersebut adalah Allah merupakan wali bagi orang-orang beriman. Kedudukan Allah sebagai wali menunjukkan adanya hubungan kedekatan, perlindungan, dan pertolongan antara Allah dengan hamba-Nya.

Menurutnya, pemahaman ini sekaligus mengoreksi cara pandang yang memisahkan aktivitas manusia dari keterlibatan Allah. Dalam kehidupan sehari-hari, seseorang bisa saja merasa bahwa keberhasilan bisnis sepenuhnya berasal dari perhitungan modal, strategi, dan kerja kerasnya sendiri.

“Seakan-akan untung dari perdagangan kita itu hasil dari berdagang. Hubungannya dengan Allah mana?” ungkapnya memberikan ilustrasi.

Padahal, lanjut Ustadi, keberhasilan seseorang juga berkaitan dengan kemudahan dan kepercayaan yang diberikan Allah. Dalam kegiatan bisnis, misalnya, seseorang dapat memperoleh keuntungan karena mendapatkan kepercayaan dari orang lain. Kepercayaan itu pun berkaitan dengan pertolongan Allah yang menutupi berbagai kekurangan manusia.

Ia mencontohkan seseorang yang produknya dipercaya konsumen karena memiliki pelayanan yang baik. Kepercayaan tersebut menjadi salah satu faktor yang mendukung keberhasilan usahanya. Karena itu, manusia perlu menyadari bahwa kemampuan dan usaha yang dimiliki tetap berada dalam keterhubungan dengan pertolongan Allah.

Kesadaran tersebut juga perlu dibawa ketika seseorang menghadapi kegagalan. Ustadi menjelaskan bahwa ketika usaha tidak berjalan sesuai harapan, orang beriman perlu melakukan introspeksi dan evaluasi. Ia perlu melihat kembali apa yang kurang tepat, kemudian memperbaiki dan meningkatkan kualitas usahanya.

Lebih jauh, Ustadi menghubungkan kedekatan dengan Allah dengan pembentukan karakter manusia. Ia memberikan ilustrasi tentang seorang guru yang memiliki dua murid dengan kemampuan akademik hampir sama, tetapi berbeda dalam sikap. Murid yang memiliki sikap baik dan menghormati gurunya lebih layak memperoleh kepercayaan ketika keduanya memiliki capaian akademik yang setara.

Menurutnya, ilustrasi tersebut menggambarkan bagaimana kepercayaan dan kasih sayang dapat diberikan kepada seseorang yang menunjukkan kepantasan melalui sikapnya.

“Kalau kita kepada Allah, maka kita lakukan bukan yang minimalis, tetapi kita lakukan yang terbaik,” tegasnya.

Ustadi menekankan bahwa kedekatan dengan Allah semestinya mendorong manusia meningkatkan kualitas perbuatan. Orang beriman perlu berusaha menjadi pribadi yang lebih baik sehingga pantas memperoleh rahmat dan kebaikan dari Allah.

Dalam penjelasannya, ia juga mengingatkan bahwa setan merupakan wali bagi orang-orang yang tidak beriman. Sifat setaniah dapat melekat pada manusia maupun jin, yakni segala sesuatu yang membisikkan keburukan dan mengarahkan manusia menjauh dari jalan Allah.

Bahkan, Ustadi mengingatkan bahwa benda-benda dalam kehidupan modern, seperti telepon genggam, dapat menjadi sarana yang melalaikan apabila penggunaannya membuat manusia menyimpang dari istiqamah kepada Allah.

Karena itu, ia mengajak jamaah menjaga hubungan dengan Allah dalam seluruh aktivitas kehidupan sekaligus mewaspadai berbagai hal yang dapat menjauhkan manusia dari kebenaran.

Kesadaran Bertuhan Harus Hadir dalam Setiap Aktivitas Kehidupan

MUHAMMADIYAH.OR.ID, YOGYAKARTA—Ketua Majelis Tarjih dan Tajdid Pimpinan Pusat Muhammadiyah Ustadi Hamsah menjelaskan makna aulia dalam Surah Ali Imran ayat 28 yang memuat larangan bagi orang beriman menjadikan orang-orang kafir sebagai sekutu dengan mengesampingkan sesama orang beriman.

Menurutnya, pemahaman terhadap ayat tersebut perlu memperhatikan makna kata aulia sesuai konteks penggunaannya dalam Al-Qur’an.

Hal itu disampaikan Ustadi dalam Pengajian Tarjih pada Rabu (11/11). Dalam kajiannya, ia menjelaskan bahwa kata wali atau aulia memiliki beragam makna. Secara harfiah, kata tersebut mengandung pengertian kedekatan. Maknanya dapat berkembang menjadi teman dekat, pelindung, penolong, pembela, pemimpin, hingga sekutu.

Ustadi merujuk pada Tafsir At-Tanwir yang mengelompokkan makna aulia ke dalam 3 klasifikasi, yaitu al-qurb (kedekatan), an-nusrah (pertolongan atau perlindungan), dan as-sulthan (kewenangan atau kekuasaan). Dari ketiga klasifikasi tersebut, ia menekankan bahwa makna mendasar yang dapat ditarik adalah sekutu.

“Janganlah orang-orang beriman menjadikan orang kafir sebagai sekutu,” jelasnya ketika menerangkan kandungan Surah Ali Imran ayat 28.

Menurut Ustadi, persekutuan mengandung hubungan yang lebih luas daripada sekadar kedekatan personal. Di dalamnya terdapat kepercayaan, kerja sama, perlindungan, kesetiaan, dan dukungan. Hubungan semacam itu dapat membentuk pola patronase antara pihak-pihak yang terlibat.

Ia kemudian menguraikan sejumlah pesan dari pemaknaan tersebut. Pertama, Allah merupakan wali bagi orang-orang beriman. Karena itu, orang beriman harus menempatkan Allah sebagai tempat bergantung dan tidak menjadikan pihak lain sebagai sekutu dalam penghambaan kepada-Nya.

Kedua, hubungan manusia dengan Allah harus senantiasa terpelihara. Ustadi menjelaskan bahwa kehidupan orang beriman selalu memiliki keterhubungan dengan Allah, termasuk ketika menjalankan aktivitas ekonomi dan pekerjaan sehari-hari.

Ketiga, orang beriman perlu menyadari bahwa setan merupakan wali bagi orang-orang yang tidak beriman. Setan dalam pengertian ini juga mencakup sifat-sifat yang mengarahkan manusia menjauh dari kebenaran.

Melalui penjelasan tersebut, Ustadi mengajak jamaah memahami Surah Ali Imran ayat 28 dengan memperhatikan kedalaman makna aulia. Pemahaman itu menjadi landasan bagi orang beriman dalam menentukan hubungan, loyalitas, dan pihak yang dijadikan tempat bergantung.

Apple’s latest lineup of smart home devices, Home View, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod 2, offers a mix of sleek design, advanced features, and ecosystem integration. The Home View, for example, boasts a 7-inch liquid retina display and adaptive interface but lacks third-party app support, limiting its functionality. Similarly, the HomePod 2 delivers impressive sound quality and stereo pairing options, while the Apple TV 4K introduces hands-free Siri and A19 chip-powered AI, as explored by Better Creating.

Dive into this breakdown to understand how these devices perform in real-world scenarios. Discover the Home View’s multi-user customization and Siri’s whisper-responsive commands, the Apple TV 4K’s surround sound setup with HomePods, and the HomePod 2’s role in multi-room audio systems. This explainer highlights key strengths and limitations, helping you assess whether Apple’s smart home ecosystem fits your needs.

The Apple Home View features a 7-inch liquid retina display and integrates well with Apple’s ecosystem, but its lack of third-party app support and an app store limits functionality, with unsupported widgets proving frustrating in testing. Siri on the Home View can respond to whispered commands from up to 2 meters away and assist with tasks like cooking using on-device intelligence, but the interface is described as unintuitive, and the bezel design feels outdated. The Apple TV 4K, powered by the A19 chip, introduces hands-free Siri activation, a Siri AI beta with natural conversation capabilities, and seamless integration with other Apple devices, making it a standout upgrade for $299. The HomePod 2 delivers “super loud” and “super clean” sound with “lovely bass,” supports stereo pairing, and integrates with the Apple TV and Home View for multi-room audio setups, automatically adjusting timing and levels for optimal performance. While the Apple Home View, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod 2 offer a cohesive smart home experience for Apple users, the high cost and certain limitations, such as the Home View’s restricted functionality, may deter those outside the Apple ecosystem.

The Apple Home View is a new addition to Apple’s smart home lineup, featuring a 7-inch liquid retina display with an adaptive design inspired by the Apple Watch interface. Users can link their Apple accounts to access features like podcasts, Spotify, and Find My. However, the absence of an app store and third-party app support, such as Claude or ChatGPT (available in CarPlay), restricts its functionality.

Widgets for unsupported apps appear but cannot be used, which proved frustrating in testing. For example, selecting the Claude widget results in an “unavailable” message.

The Home View supports up to six users, each able to customize widgets and views. Security settings allow access to be limited to the user, anyone using the device, or recognized individuals. However, Siri’s access to personal data like messages or calendars requires each user to have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad signed into the same Apple account linked to the Home View.

Conversations started on the Home View hub also appear on the connected iPhone. While the device integrates well with Apple’s ecosystem, its compatibility with external devices is limited. For instance, it can detect a UG Green NAS but only offers a music menu, with no option to check or send files.

Voice control is a standout feature. Siri responds to whispered commands from up to 2 meters away, performing tasks like providing weather updates, managing calendars, playing music, and finding recipes. The updated Siri AI uses on-device intelligence to assist with cooking, recognizing recipes and guiding users through the process.

However, the lack of a dedicated Siri app on the Home View and an unintuitive interface, featuring a secondary menu described as “almost looks wrong”, detract from the experience. Additionally, the bezel design feels outdated compared to other Apple products.

The Home View comes in two versions: a tabletop model with a woofer and passive radiators for enhanced bass and higher output, and a wall-mounted version with two full-range drivers in the display. Both versions are priced the same, which raised questions during testing given their differing sound capabilities. Apple recommends the tabletop version for users prioritizing bass performance.

Accessibility features include live captions for FaceTime calls, voice-over settings, intercom alarms, and a ring light system for face recognition, similar to a feature introduced on the MacBook. Apple has also partnered with third-party home tech providers, including LG, to expand its ecosystem with devices like doorbells, security cameras, and intercoms.

The Apple TV 4K introduces several upgrades, including the A19 chip for on-device AI and built-in microphones for hands-free Siri activation. Users can now say “Hey Siri” to control the device without pressing a button.

The Siri AI beta, accessible through the settings menu, supports natural conversation, full-screen search results, and additional content details. Activating this feature requires an iPhone or iPad running version 27.2. To enable the Siri AI beta, users navigate to General > Siri in the Apple TV settings.

While the Apple TV 4K retains the same physical dimensions as its predecessor, the status light has been relocated to the center to accommodate the new microphones. The remote now features precise Find My functionality, making it easier to locate. Priced at $299, the device also offers a software update that allows older Apple TV models to access the new Siri AI, though without voice control or the processing power of the A19 chip.

The Apple TV 4K integrates seamlessly with other Apple devices, such as the HomePod 2, and supports advanced audio configurations. Users can create surround sound systems with up to four HomePod Mini 2s or second-generation HomePods, with matching front and rear speaker pairs required. To set up surround sound with an existing stereo pair, users must first unpair the speakers.

The system automatically calibrates timing and levels for the room, delivering impressive sound quality. Beyond home cinema setups, the Apple TV can also function in a desk configuration, connecting to a monitor via HDMI and using Ethernet for network connectivity.

The HomePod 2 introduces new color options and supports stereo pairing, allowing users to create immersive audio setups. The speakers integrate with the Apple TV and Home View, enabling audio playback across different rooms or systems via the “play to” feature. Sound quality is described as “super loud,” “super clean,” and featuring “lovely bass.” The new speakers are compatible with other Apple devices, allowing users to gradually build a comprehensive sound system.

In a home cinema configuration, larger HomePods can be paired at the front with Mini 2s at the rear. The speakers automatically adjust their timing and levels to suit the room, ensuring a balanced audio experience. For optimal performance, the front and rear speaker pairs must match.

The intercom feature on the Home View adds further functionality, allowing users to send messages to specific rooms or throughout the house. Additionally, the Home View includes sound settings for intercom alarms, enhancing its usability in multi-room setups.

The Home View, Apple TV 4K, and HomePod 2 represent a significant investment, especially when purchased together. While the Home View offers sleek design and strong integration with the Apple ecosystem, its limited functionality and outdated bezel design may deter some users. The host suggested waiting for Apple to expand its features before committing to the Home View.

The Apple TV 4K, however, is described as “absolutely brilliant” and a worthwhile upgrade for those without a recent model. Its voice control, AI capabilities, and seamless integration with other Apple devices make it a compelling addition to an Apple-centric home setup. Similarly, the HomePod 2 earns praise for its excellent sound quality and versatility, making it an appealing choice for users seeking to enhance their audio experience.

For those already invested in the Apple ecosystem, these devices offer a cohesive and well-executed smart home experience. However, for users less entrenched in Apple’s ecosystem, the high cost and certain limitations may make these products less justifiable.

AI’s influence on academia is growing, but not without complications. Some journals have been caught publishing AI-generated papers under the names of respected academics without their consent, raising serious ethical concerns. In one case, a professor’s name was removed from a fraudulent paper, only for it to reappear under a different author. To combat this misuse, researchers are encouraged to set up alerts to monitor unauthorized publications, as highlighted by Andy Stapleton.

Explore how AI is reshaping academic norms, from accelerating scientific discoveries to challenging traditional education systems. Learn about groundbreaking achievements like AlphaGenome 2 replicating months of lab work in minutes, and understand the implications of AI-assisted cheating on university assessments. This feature also examines how institutions like Harvard and Chicago are navigating these shifts, offering insights into the evolving balance between innovation and integrity in higher education.

Some lesser-known academic journals are reportedly publishing AI-generated papers under the names of established professors without their consent, allegedly to boost credibility. Affected academics have advised setting up alerts to monitor unauthorized use of their names. Google DeepMind’s AI model, AlphaGenome 2, replicated key aspects of a scientific discovery on inflammatory bowel disease in just 30 minutes, compared to 18 months of traditional lab work, though human oversight remains necessary to mitigate risks like hallucinations and errors. Anthropic’s analysis of over 200,000 Claude research sessions found that researchers primarily use AI for assistive tasks like data analysis, writing, and data gathering, with lower adoption rates in fields such as library sciences and religion. AI-assisted cheating is reportedly undermining higher education, with students using large language models to complete assessments quickly and achieve comparable grades. Universities are being urged to implement systemic changes to maintain the credibility of degrees. Harvard and the University of Chicago are leading AI education initiatives, with Harvard introducing an AI guidance tool for educators and Chicago launching an AI-free writing course for first-year students to preserve traditional writing skills.

A troubling trend has emerged in academic publishing: some lesser-known journals are releasing AI-generated papers under the names of established professors without their consent. In one instance, a professor discovered such a paper and had their name removed, only for the paper to be republished under a different name, which was later changed again.

Affected academics have stated, “I confirmed that I did not write the paper, was not involved in its submission, and did not authorize the use of my name. I was also unaware of its existence until the email.” This misuse of names appears aimed at boosting the credibility of these journals by associating them with prominent researchers.

To reduce such risks, academics are advised to set up alerts, such as Google Scholar notifications, to monitor unauthorized use of their names in publications.

AI is showing its potential to transform scientific research, as demonstrated by a comparison between traditional lab work and AI-driven methods. In 2024, researchers identified a new driver of inflammatory bowel disease through 18 months of conventional lab experiments. In contrast, Google DeepMind’s AI model, AlphaGenome 2, replicated key aspects of this discovery in just 30 minutes, without any physical lab work.

While this rapid verification is promising, testing highlighted that AI models like AlphaGenome 2 still require human oversight due to risks such as hallucinations and errors. However, as a complementary tool for validation, AI offers significant potential to support traditional research methods.

Anthropic analyzed over 200,000 Claude research sessions to understand how scientists are using AI tools like Claude. The analysis revealed that data analysis is the most common application, particularly in fields such as medicine, computer science, and engineering. In contrast, disciplines like library sciences, nutrition, and religion showed lower adoption rates.

The study also found that researchers primarily use AI in assistive or collaborative roles, with fewer relying on it autonomously or avoiding it entirely. This suggests that AI is most effective when augmenting tasks like data analysis, writing, and data gathering, rather than replacing them outright.

AI-assisted cheating is posing a serious threat to the credibility of higher education. Students have reportedly used large language models to complete assessments in minutes, achieving grades comparable to peers who completed the work independently. Despite detection efforts, tools like OpenAI’s watermarking and Claude’s detection systems have proven unreliable.

The Office for Students has warned universities that they could face fines if they fail to address this issue. Institutions are being urged to help students develop AI skills while maintaining confidence in the value of degrees. However, many universities still rely on unsupervised assessments, which are no longer effective measures of learning. The host argued that systemic changes are needed to prevent students from earning degrees without genuine learning.

The host also suggested that universities consider implementing a full AI-free year before allowing students to use AI in controlled ways. This approach would resemble past practices, such as requiring one math exam with a calculator and one without, though it is unclear if such methods are still in use today.

Two leading universities are taking proactive steps to address AI’s impact on education. Harvard’s Graduate School of Education has introduced a tool designed to provide AI guidance tailored to different age groups. This tool offers quick takes, recommendations, and insights into how AI might support or hinder human development at various stages. Features include guidance on key developmental processes and milestones for different age groups.

While the tool is based on hypotheses rather than established facts, it is seen as a valuable resource for educators. Meanwhile, the University of Chicago has launched an AI-free writing course for all first-year students. Administered through the university’s writing center, this initiative aims to preserve traditional writing skills while exploring new practices and technologies. The center is also developing additional writing labs and campus partnerships to support both students and faculty.

AI’s expanding role in academia presents both opportunities and challenges. Tools like AlphaGenome 2 demonstrate the potential to accelerate scientific discovery, while platforms like Claude are reshaping how researchers approach data analysis and writing. However, the misuse of AI in academic publishing and assessments highlights the urgent need for ethical safeguards and systemic reforms.

Universities must balance fostering AI literacy with preserving the integrity of education. Initiatives like Harvard’s developmental tool and Chicago’s AI-free writing courses are early steps in this direction. Yet, the broader academic system faces a critical challenge: adapting to AI’s capabilities without compromising the core values of learning and research.

Apple has introduced its first MacBook with a touchscreen, blending touch functionality with macOS while retaining its traditional keyboard and trackpad design. This move reflects Apple’s measured approach to innovation, balancing new input methods with usability. The touchscreen offers added convenience in certain scenarios, but macOS remains fundamentally optimized for cursor-based interaction. This creates a hybrid experience that showcases both the potential and the limitations of touch integration within a desktop operating system. The video below from Mac Vince gives us more details.

Direct-Bonded Panel: Integrated straight into the tandem OLED PROLED XDR screen to minimize input latency and keep visuals razor-sharp. Context-Aware UI Scaling: macOS dynamically expands small interface targets like window control buttons and dropdown spacing when a finger approaches. Hybrid Navigation: Complements standard trackpad and keyboard workflows, excelling at quick scrolling, media playback, and running native iOS apps. Productivity Focus: Preserves its core cursor-centric architecture instead of forcing a touch-first interface compromise.

The touchscreen MacBook extends familiar macOS gestures, such as swiping between desktops, pinching to zoom and dragging windows, directly to the display. Borrowing from iOS and iPadOS, Apple has incorporated gestures like pulling down to access the Control Center or refreshing a webpage with a swipe. These additions aim to make the touchscreen experience intuitive for users already familiar with Apple’s ecosystem.

However, macOS’s core design still prioritizes cursor-based interaction. Many interface elements, such as small buttons, dropdown menus and text fields, remain optimized for precise mouse or trackpad input rather than finger taps. This creates a learning curve for users expecting a seamless transition between touch and traditional input methods. While the touchscreen adds a layer of convenience, its integration into macOS feels more like an enhancement than a fundamental shift in how the system operates.

The addition of a touchscreen opens up new possibilities for specific tasks and workflows, offering distinct advantages in certain use cases:

Despite these benefits, the touchscreen is not a universal solution. Many macOS apps, including Apple’s own software, lack full gesture support. For example, Final Cut Pro does not support pinch-to-zoom, limiting the practicality of touch for professional workflows. These gaps highlight the challenges of adapting macOS to a touch-first environment while maintaining its productivity-focused identity.

One of the most significant obstacles in integrating touch into macOS is its interface design. Unlike iOS or iPadOS, macOS was not originally built with touch in mind, leading to several usability challenges:

These design challenges underscore the need for a more unified approach to touch interaction across Apple’s ecosystem. Without significant adjustments, macOS risks feeling like a compromise between touch and traditional input methods rather than a fully integrated experience.

To address some of these hurdles, Apple has introduced adaptive interface features designed to improve usability. For example, when users touch certain elements like buttons or menus, they expand slightly to make them easier to interact with. This contextual adjustment demonstrates Apple’s commitment to refining the touchscreen experience without compromising macOS’s core functionality.

Apple is also encouraging developers to adopt similar adaptive designs in their apps. Features like larger touch targets, gesture-based navigation and simplified interfaces can enhance the touchscreen experience. However, widespread adoption will take time, as developers must balance the needs of both touch and traditional input users. The success of these adaptive solutions will depend on how effectively Apple and third-party developers collaborate to optimize apps for hybrid input methods.

The touchscreen on macOS is best understood as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for the keyboard, trackpad, or mouse. Apple has deliberately avoided oversimplifying macOS to prioritize touch, preserving its identity as a productivity-focused operating system. While the touchscreen shows potential, macOS is not yet fully optimized for touch-first use.

For now, the touchscreen serves as an optional enhancement, useful in specific scenarios but not essential for everyday workflows. Apple’s cautious approach ensures that macOS retains its core functionality while gradually exploring the possibilities of touch integration. As developers and users adapt to this new input method, the potential for a more cohesive and versatile touch experience on macOS remains an intriguing prospect. However, significant refinements and a more unified design philosophy will be necessary to fully realize this vision.

RAID configurations have long been a cornerstone of data redundancy, but SSDs introduce unique challenges that can undermine their reliability. Unlike mechanical hard drives, which fail randomly due to wear on moving parts, SSDs often fail predictably based on write endurance and other factors like heat or electrical wear. This predictability, combined with the uniform workloads typical in RAID arrays, can lead to synchronized failures, as demonstrated by the near-simultaneous breakdown of two 240 GB Kingston SSDs in a TrueNAS SCALE server. These risks are explored in detail by SpaceRex.

Understand how to navigate these vulnerabilities with practical strategies and insights. You’ll learn why enterprise-grade SSDs with higher DWPD ratings are better suited for RAID, how RAID types like RAID Z1 or RAID F1 can stagger failure risks, and why diversifying drive purchases can reduce batch-related issues. This explainer also emphasizes the importance of robust backups, ensuring you’re prepared for worst-case scenarios.

The near-simultaneous failure of two 240 GB Kingston SSDs in a TrueNAS SCALE server after four years of light usage highlights the risk of synchronized SSD failures in RAID configurations. SSDs fail differently from mechanical drives, with primary failure modes tied to write endurance and secondary risks like heat, electrical wear, and manufacturing defects, which can lead to correlated failures in RAID arrays. RAID redundancy is less effective for SSDs due to their uniform workload, increasing the likelihood of simultaneous failures, especially in larger arrays or without hot spares, emphasizing the need for robust backup systems. Mitigation strategies include diversifying drive purchases, periodically swapping hot spares, using RAID types like RAID Z1 or RAID F1 to stagger writes, and performing burn-in testing, though none are foolproof. The TrueNAS failure demonstrated the importance of regular backups and proactive monitoring of SSD lifespan through SMART data, as RAID alone cannot prevent data loss from simultaneous SSD failures.

The near-simultaneous failure of two 240 GB Kingston SSDs within 16 days highlights a significant vulnerability in RAID configurations using SSDs. These drives, used as boot drives in a TrueNAS SCALE server, had been in operation for four years under minimal workloads. Despite this light usage, their synchronized failure reveals the unique risks SSDs pose in RAID setups.

SSDs fail in ways distinct from mechanical hard drives. While traditional drives fail randomly due to wear on moving parts, SSD failures are often more predictable. Their primary failure mode is tied to write endurance: each flash cell has a limited number of writes it can handle before wearing out. Enterprise SSDs are rated by DWPD (drive writes per day), indicating how many times the entire drive can be overwritten during its warranty period.

Secondary failure risks also exist for SSDs. Heat, electrical wear, and manufacturing defects can lead to simultaneous failures, especially in RAID arrays. Unlike mechanical drives, where variability in wear reduces the chance of synchronized failures, SSDs in RAID configurations are more vulnerable due to their uniform workload. Enterprise-grade SSDs are less prone to this issue but are not immune.

RAID redundancy works well for mechanical hard drives because their failures are typically random and uncorrelated. Mechanical drives from the same batch can have lifespans ranging from three to eight years. In contrast, SSDs in RAID arrays experience identical read and write patterns, increasing the likelihood of synchronized failures. This was evident with the two Kingston SSDs, which failed after four years of identical usage.

The risk is even higher in larger SSD arrays. For example, an 18-drive array with three groups of RAID 5 (six drives each) could face simultaneous failures across multiple drives due to their uniform workload. Such failures can overwhelm hot spares and RAID’s redundancy mechanisms, leaving backups and failover systems as the only safeguards. If multiple drives fail within a short period, such as 30 days, hot spares may not suffice, underscoring the need for robust backup strategies.

Even RAID 10, known for its strong redundancy, cannot fully protect against simultaneous failures caused by the same underlying issue. This limitation highlights the need for additional safeguards when deploying SSDs in RAID configurations.

Several strategies can reduce the risk of simultaneous SSD failures:

While these measures can mitigate risks, they are not foolproof. It is critical to remember that RAID is not a backup solution. A comprehensive backup and replication system is essential to protect against simultaneous drive failures.

DRAM-less SSDs, such as the Kingston drives in this case, are not recommended for critical data storage due to their limitations. However, they may be suitable for boot drives if restoring and backing up the system is straightforward and non-critical.

The failure of the two Kingston SSDs highlights the importance of understanding SSD limitations in RAID configurations. These drives, described as “C-tier” and lacking DRAM, were considered adequate for boot drives but not for critical storage. When the first drive failed, an alert was issued 16 days before the second failure, warning that redundancy had been lost. However, the absence of a hot spare and the short interval between failures left the system vulnerable.

TrueNAS SCALE minimizes wear on boot drives by performing limited reads and writes. Historically, it could even run from a flash drive, dismounting the boot volume after startup and operating from RAM. The ZFS file system further reduces drive activity by caching data in RAM. This design explains why the boot drives experienced minimal wear despite four years of continuous operation.

Rebuilding the boot pool was straightforward, taking just 1.5 hours. The TrueNAS configuration file is small and easily backed up as a zip file, simplifying recovery. The failure provided an opportunity to reset the NAS to its default configuration. However, had the failure occurred in a data pool rather than a boot pool, the consequences could have been far more severe. This underscores the critical need for regular backups and a clear recovery plan.

SSDs provide lifespan data through SMART monitoring, which reports the percentage of life remaining. Regularly checking this data can help predict failures and schedule replacements proactively. Repairing an entire system is far more challenging than maintaining RAID arrays, making proactive monitoring essential.

Despite the challenges, recovery from the SSD failures was successful. The system was restored from backup, and other SSDs were replaced without significant difficulty. However, the incident caused a brief outage, illustrating the potential impact of simultaneous SSD failures.

The simultaneous failure of two SSDs in a RAID configuration highlights the unique risks SSDs pose. While generally reliable, SSDs are susceptible to synchronized failures due to consistent failure modes and uniform workloads in RAID arrays. Strategies like diversifying drive purchases, staggering usage times, and selecting RAID types that distribute writes unevenly can help mitigate these risks, but they cannot eliminate them entirely.

The key takeaway is that RAID is not a substitute for a backup. Even with careful planning, simultaneous SSD failures can occur, and only a robust backup and replication system can safeguard critical data. For those relying on SSDs in RAID, understanding these risks and preparing accordingly is essential to prevent catastrophic data loss.

What happens when you give an advanced AI model a simple idea and let it handle the development process? The early projects created with Claude Fable 5.2 offer a fascinating glimpse of what’s becoming possible. From fully playable video games and detailed 3D environments to cinematic animations, engineering simulations, and experimental hardware designs, creators are pushing the model well beyond traditional coding tasks.

Some of the most impressive demonstrations involve remarkably little initial guidance. One developer reportedly created a first-person shooter in eight hours using just three casual sentences, while another used a single prompt to produce a 4K animated film, with the AI independently arranging GPU resources for rendering. Other projects include an interactive recreation of Earth, a virtual journey through eight dreamlike worlds, and a detailed recreation of Istanbul built primarily through code.

The two videos explored in this article bring together a wide selection of these early experiments, offering a closer look at the creative possibilities, technical achievements, and practical limitations of Fable 5.2. Rather than focusing on individual prompts, they reveal how AI is beginning to take on more of the work involved in designing, building, and refining complex digital projects.

Playable games and interactive worlds: Fable 5.2 is being used to develop first-person shooters, adventure games, browser experiences, and detailed virtual environments from relatively simple instructions. 3D modelling and engineering: Creators are experimenting with complex mechanical systems, vehicle models, animated characters, interactive simulations, and prototype electronic devices. AI-generated films and animation: The model can coordinate scripts, scenes, visual assets, rendering workflows, and external AI tools to help produce sophisticated animated content. Greater autonomy: Some demonstrations show Fable 5.2 managing lengthy development processes, coordinating sub-agents, troubleshooting problems, and refining projects with limited human intervention. Important practical limitations: Although the results can be impressive, development costs, processing times, technical imperfections, and the need for human oversight remain significant considerations.

One of the most striking developments highlighted in the videos is Fable 5.2’s ability to create interactive games and virtual experiences. Rather than producing isolated pieces of code, the model can work across multiple aspects of development, including environments, gameplay mechanics, visual assets, character behaviour, and user interactions.

An example is Saltline, a first-person shooter developed by Anthropic employee Felix Riesberg. According to its creator, the game was built in approximately eight hours from three short sentences, with the model generating the graphics, textures, sounds, and gameplay elements. The project reportedly cost around $550, illustrating both the potential of autonomous AI development and the resources these experiments can consume.

Other demonstrations take a completely different creative approach. Kevin’s dreamlike boat journey allows players to travel through eight atmospheric worlds, combining lighting, environmental design, and gentle exploration into a meditative browser experience. Meanwhile, the adventure game Lantern Wake introduces interactive characters, missions, combat, and exploration, showing how AI-assisted development can make increasingly ambitious projects accessible to creators without extensive experience using traditional game development tools.

The videos also feature experimental browser games, underwater environments, enhanced versions of classic arcade concepts, and interactive worlds populated by AI-controlled characters. Together, these projects demonstrate how Fable 5.2 can help turn a creative concept into something users can actually explore and interact with.

Beyond conventional games, Fable 5.2 is being used to generate elaborate three-dimensional scenes and environments that would ordinarily require considerable modelling, programming, and design work.

Several examples demonstrate the model’s ability to construct detailed locations using code rather than relying entirely on existing assets. These include a recreation of Istanbul featuring the Golden Horn, Galata Bridge, ferries, pedestrians, and adjustable lighting, alongside an ambitious browser-based representation of Earth built using voxel graphics and real-world geographic data.

Other creators have experimented with architectural visualisations, immersive rooftop environments, and interconnected 3D worlds that can be explored through portals. One particularly ambitious project reportedly generated more than 200 connected worlds during an extended development session.

These demonstrations are interesting not simply because of their visual quality, but because of the number of interconnected tasks involved. Creating a convincing virtual environment requires the model to consider geometry, materials, lighting, scale, animation, and interaction, often within the same project.

Not every result is technically perfect. Some demonstrations contain collision problems, unusual character behaviour, or visual inconsistencies. Nevertheless, the speed at which increasingly elaborate environments can be prototyped represents an important development for independent creators, designers, and game developers.

Another important area explored in the videos is the application of Fable 5.2 to engineering, mechanical design, and interactive simulations. These demonstrations move beyond visual presentation to examine whether AI can generate models and systems with meaningful behaviour.

Projects include an interactive car differential that demonstrates how mechanical components transfer motion, a detailed Bugatti Tourbillon model created in Blender, and an animated zombie hand capable of performing complex movements while maintaining convincing joint mechanics.

Other experiments explore interactive physics and natural movement. One demonstration simulates a flock of birds responding dynamically to hand gestures, while another features a water balloon being pierced by a bullet, with the resulting animation attempting to reproduce the behaviour of the water as the balloon breaks.

The videos also highlight more educational applications. In one project, sketches from Leonardo da Vinci’s notebooks are transformed into interactive three-dimensional machines, allowing viewers to explore the mechanical concepts behind centuries-old drawings. Another recreates an animated journey through microscopic structures to illustrate Zeno’s paradox.

Fable 5.2 has also been used in experimental hardware development, including a Tamagotchi-style electronic device with a circuit board, physical enclosure, and visual design.

Although these examples should not be confused with fully validated engineering products, they suggest that AI could become increasingly useful for rapid prototyping, technical visualisation, educational demonstrations, and early-stage product development.

The two videos also showcase how Fable 5.2 can be used to produce animation, short films, music videos, and other forms of visual storytelling.

Several creators have experimented with giving the model a broad creative objective and allowing it to develop the concept, organise scenes, generate assets, and coordinate production tools. In some cases, Fable 5.2 works alongside specialised image, video, and music-generation systems, acting as a central coordinator rather than directly generating every element itself.

One demonstration involved asking the model to create the video of its dreams. The resulting production combined scripted scenes, generated imagery, video sequences, and music into a surreal animated experience. Other examples include a frozen landscape transforming into spring, chalk drawings brought to life, dystopian music videos, and animations constructed frame by frame using JavaScript.

A particularly interesting example involved the creation of a 4K animated short film using Blender. The creator reported that Fable 5.2 generated the scene and arranged access to ten GPUs for rendering, handling additional resource requests when some attempts failed. The reported rendering bill was approximately $5.75, although that figure does not represent the complete cost of the AI development process.

These projects demonstrate a significant shift in how creative software can be used. Instead of manually controlling every modelling, animation, and rendering operation, creators can increasingly describe the desired outcome and let an AI system coordinate portions of the production workflow.

Human creative judgement remains important, however. Some of the demonstrations involved selecting between alternative outputs, improving prompts, correcting visual problems, or combining multiple AI tools to achieve a satisfactory result.

Perhaps the most significant capability illustrated by these projects is Fable 5.2’s ability to work through extended, multi-stage tasks.

Traditional AI coding assistants typically help with individual programming problems, file modifications, or specific development requests. The demonstrations featured in the videos suggest a broader workflow in which AI can plan an approach, generate code, test results, identify problems, and continue refining a project over time.

Some creators have used the model to coordinate specialised sub-agents responsible for separate aspects of development, such as modelling, code generation, quality checks, and visual refinement.

Anthropic has also described much larger internal experiments, including a prototype operating system reportedly created over eight days with more than a thousand cooperating sub-agents. Such projects are experimental rather than examples of ordinary consumer workflows, but they illustrate the direction in which autonomous development systems are moving.

The ability to coordinate tools is particularly relevant to creative production. Across the featured projects, Fable 5.2 is shown working with Blender, browser technologies, rendering resources, and other AI services to complete tasks that would otherwise require multiple specialised applications and substantial manual coordination.

Although the demonstrations are impressive, the videos also raise important questions about cost, efficiency, and reliability. Some experiments were completed in minutes and cost relatively little, while larger projects required hours of processing and substantially higher expenditure. A complex spreadsheet application featured in one demonstration reportedly required around 50 hours of development and cost approximately $11,700, with its creator acknowledging that not every feature had been fully tested.

Other comparisons suggest that Fable 5.2 does not necessarily offer the best value for every task. In two head-to-head development experiments discussed in one video, Opus 5.5 was less expensive, although Fable sometimes delivered stronger visuals or completed the work more quickly.

The demonstrations also reveal the difference between an attractive prototype and a finished, reliable application. Visual imperfections, unexpected physics, incomplete functionality, and unverified features remain common challenges. For simpler tasks such as routine writing, scripting, or straightforward programming, less expensive models may still be sufficient. The strongest argument for using Fable 5.2 appears to be its ability to tackle more ambitious, interconnected creative and technical projects where autonomous planning and tool coordination offer meaningful advantages.

Taken together, the examples in both videos provide a useful overview of how rapidly AI-assisted creation is evolving.

The most important development is not that Fable 5.2 can generate a game, an animation, or a detailed 3D model in isolation. It is that the model can increasingly combine these capabilities into larger workflows, handling multiple stages of a project and coordinating the tools needed to produce a usable result.

For developers, this could mean faster prototyping and experimentation. For designers and filmmakers, it creates new ways to explore complex visual ideas without manually producing every asset. For engineers and educators, it opens up possibilities for interactive demonstrations, simulations, and early-stage technical concepts.

There are still meaningful limitations involving cost, reliability, accuracy, and the need for human supervision. The projects shown in these videos are best understood as demonstrations of what is becoming possible, rather than proof that AI can independently deliver production-ready software or professionally validated designs in every situation.

Nevertheless, Claude Fable 5.2 offers a compelling glimpse of a future in which creating sophisticated digital experiences begins with describing an idea rather than manually building every component. The two videos provide a broad look at that emerging potential, from experimental games and animated films to engineering models and increasingly autonomous development workflows.

The Xbox Nano Controller presents a compact and lightweight alternative to standard Xbox controllers, weighing just over 100 grams, nearly one-third the weight of its full-sized counterpart. It also considers the barriers to adoption, from cost concerns to regulatory gaps, and what it will take for these facilities to support, rather than strain, the grid.

The rapid expansion of AI data centers is raising concerns about their impact on electricity grids. These facilities consumed approximately 460TWh of electricity in 2024, comparable to France’s total consumption. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), this demand could more than double by 2030, reaching 1,000TWh, and potentially climb to 1,300TWh by 2035.

This growth would account for about one-tenth of global electricity demand increases over the next decade. However, the unique operational characteristics of AI data centers present challenges that could strain grids in new ways.

AI data centers differ significantly from traditional ones in electricity consumption. While traditional facilities operate with steady, predictable loads, AI workloads can cause rapid demand fluctuations, sometimes within seconds. This variability is distinct from renewable energy intermittency, which can be forecasted based on weather. Instead, AI data centers can shift electricity demand “on demand,” creating challenges for grid operators tasked with maintaining real-time supply-demand balance.

Traditional data centers are often ideal utility customers due to their consistent energy use. In contrast, the dynamic and unpredictable nature of AI data centers’ demand requires new planning and operational strategies. For example, on July 10, 2024, a transmission-line failure in Northern Virginia caused dozens of data centers to switch to backup power systems, instantly removing 1.5GW of demand, equivalent to a large nuclear reactor’s output.

This sudden drop created a temporary imbalance, forcing operators to reduce generator output to stabilize grid frequency. While blackouts were avoided, the incident highlighted the challenges of integrating such large, unpredictable loads into the grid.

The growth of AI data centers demands significant infrastructure investments. Meeting their energy needs often requires utilities to build new substations, reinforce transmission lines, and upgrade local distribution networks. In some cases, entirely new power stations are needed. These upgrades can cost billions of dollars, raising questions about how the financial burden is distributed.

In some markets, large customers like data centers bear most connection costs, while in others, these expenses are shared across the wider customer base through electricity tariffs, potentially increasing costs for households and businesses.

Most grid costs are fixed, meaning infrastructure like poles, wires, and substations costs the same regardless of usage levels. Increased demand from large customers like AI data centers could theoretically improve grid economics by spreading these fixed costs over more usage. However, the location of data centers complicates this dynamic.

Clusters of facilities relying on the same substations or transmission pathways can create severe local pressure, even if the overall demand increase appears manageable. For instance, in Texas, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) reported 475GW of large loads seeking grid connections as of mid-2026, with 90% attributed to data centers. To put this into perspective, Texas’s all-time peak demand in July 2026 was about 91GW. Meeting such demand would require a grid six times larger than the state’s current capacity, an obviously unrealistic scenario.

Despite these challenges, AI data centers could help stabilize grids by adapting their demand to grid conditions, effectively becoming “dispatchable loads.” This flexibility could balance the grid, reduce costs for all users, and improve efficiency.

Emerald AI, for example, has developed software that tags workloads based on their tolerance for delays. In testing with Oracle and Phoenix, the system reportedly reduced a data center’s power use by 25% for three hours while maintaining performance targets. The software uses a digital twin to simulate operations, predicting power savings before adjustments. It can also slow chip clock speeds, pause non-urgent tasks, or shift workloads to other facilities with available capacity.

Other innovations include repurposing data center batteries, traditionally reserved for emergency backup, as active grid assets. These uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems can temporarily power data centers during grid stress, reducing demand without disrupting operations. Cooling systems can also be adjusted to pre-cool buildings, allowing reduced electricity use during peak periods.

Some utilities are exploring faster grid connections for data centers that agree to be flexible, turning their demand down when the grid is under pressure. For instance, Emerald AI is conducting a commercial-scale pilot with Silicon Valley Power in Santa Clara, involving a data center running NVIDIA’s AI workloads. While the pilot’s scale, 96 GPUs, is far smaller than a campus with 100,000 GPUs, it demonstrates the feasibility of flexible demand management.

Despite the potential benefits, most data centers are reluctant to adopt flexibility measures voluntarily. Power costs represent a small fraction of their overall expenses, and many prefer to pay more to maintain operational freedom. Some even install on-site gas turbines to bypass connection queues, often with minimal environmental oversight. Flexibility is generally seen as an inconvenience unless it offers significant advantages, such as faster grid connections, or is mandated by regulations.

Utilities, meanwhile, remain cautious about relying on flexible data centers. Concerns persist about whether these facilities will respond quickly, consistently, and repeatedly to grid requests. Building trust between utilities and data centers will be essential for scaling these solutions.

While demand for AI data centers is surging, most proposed projects are unlikely to materialize. Historical data from Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory shows that only 19% of energy projects seeking interconnection between 2000 and 2018 were completed, with just 14% of requested capacity becoming operational.

Clusters of several hundred megawatts or gigawatt-scale proposals behind the same substations and transmission pathways exacerbate these challenges, creating bottlenecks that delay or prevent projects from moving forward. Building additional power stations does not resolve certain grid challenges, such as congested substations or sudden demand changes.

It is estimated that only about 10% of proposed data centers will ultimately be built. Additionally, the current hype around data centers may surpass the energy hype of the past two decades, potentially leading to an even lower realization rate for data centers compared to energy projects. Nevertheless, the resulting increase in electricity demand will still be the largest in decades.

For over a century, electricity grids have operated on the principle that generation follows demand. AI data centers could disrupt this dynamic by becoming the first major industrial loads capable of adapting to the grid instead of requiring the grid to adapt to them. This shift has the potential to reduce costs for all users by enabling more efficient use of existing infrastructure.

However, achieving this vision will require more than technological innovation. Policymakers, regulators, and communities must implement measures that incentivize or mandate flexibility. Without such interventions, data centers are unlikely to change their behavior voluntarily. On the evidence so far, AI data centers could either exacerbate grid challenges or become one of its most valuable assets, depending on how these issues are addressed.

JAKARTA (13 November): Partai NasDem menjadikan program Wisata Edukasi Gravitasi Politik (Grawista) sebagai agenda permanen. Program yang diluncurkan dalam rangkaian HUT ke-15 Partai NasDem ini bertujuan mengenalkan sejarah, demokrasi, dan nilai-nilai kebangsaan kepada masyarakat, khususnya generasi muda.

Sekretaris Jenderal DPP Partai NasDem Hermawi Taslim mengatakan, Grawista dirancang sebagai wisata edukasi yang mengajak pengunjung mengenal Indonesia melalui berbagai fasilitas di NasDem Tower, mulai dari patung pahlawan nasional, galeri kebangsaan, hingga perpustakaan.

“Walaupun sebagai bagian dari kegiatan HUT, tapi ini akan jadi permanen. Grawista itu adalah bentuk wisata edukasi dan kebangsaan,” kata Hermawi, usai pembukaan Grawista di NasDem Tower, Jakarta Pusat, Jumat (13/11).

Partai NasDem juga berkolaborasi dengan Pemerintah Provinsi DKI Jakarta untuk menjadikan NasDem Tower sebagai salah satu destinasi wisata ibu kota. Sebanyak 15 calon pemandu wisata telah disiapkan untuk mengikuti pelatihan dan proses akreditasi Pemda DKI.

Hermawi berharap, NasDem Tower dapat masuk dalam kalender wisata Jakarta, sejajar dengan destinasi seperti Monas dan Kota Tua.

“Kita ingin mendidik generasi muda supaya lebih peduli terhadap kewarganegaraan, kebangsaan, dan kesejarahannya,” ujarnya.

Ketua Panitia Grawista yang juga Ketua Bidang Pemilih Pemula dan Milenial DPP Partai NasDem Lathifa Marina Al Anshori mengatakan, Grawista bukan sekadar kunjungan ke gedung partai. Program ini menjadi ruang belajar untuk mengenal demokrasi, kelembagaan, kepemimpinan, dan kehidupan berbangsa.

“Melalui Grawista, kami ingin mengubah cara pandang generasi muda terhadap politik dan partai politik. Bahwa partai bukan sesuatu yang harus dianggap menyeramkan, tetapi bisa menjadi ruang belajar, berdiskusi, dan memahami kehidupan berbangsa dan bernegara,” kata Lathifa.

Pada hari pertama pelaksanaan, sebanyak 55 peserta dari Kota Padang Panjang, Sumatera Barat, mengikuti kegiatan tersebut.

Pembukaan Grawista turut dihadiri pengurus DPP Partai NasDem, di antaranya Julie Sutrisno Laiskodat, Nova Harivan Paloh, dan Nining Indra Shaleh serta sejumlah anggota DPR RI dan DPRD DKI Jakarta dari Fraksi Partai NasDem. (WH/AS)

Dari Rumah Ibadah hingga Jalur Perjalanan, Kemenko PMK Kawal Kesiapan Pelayanan Nataru 2026/2027

KEMENKO PMK – Kementerian Koordinator Bidang Pembangunan Manusia dan Kebudayaan (Kemenko PMK) perkuat koordinasi lintas kementerian/lembaga dalam rangka mempersiapkan penyelenggaraan pelayanan Natal 2026 dan Tahun Baru 2027 (Nataru). Koordinasi tersebut dilaksanakan secara hybrid pada Selasa (10/11/2026).

Deputi Bidang Koordinasi Penguatan Karakter dan Jati Diri Bangsa, Kemenko PMK, Warsito menegaskan bahwa penyelenggaraan Nataru memiliki dimensi keagamaan yang memerlukan dukungan terpadu dari semua pihak. Pemerintah harus hadir secara menyeluruh untuk memastikan kesiapan peribadatan, transportasi, pelayanan kesehatan, keamanan, hingga pemenuhan kebutuhan masyarakat selama libur akhir tahun.

"Substansi utama dari kegiatan kita di akhir tahun ini adalah substansi keagamaan. Kita ingin memastikan masyarakat dapat melaksanakan ibadah Natal dengan khusyuk, menikmati libur dan perjalanan dengan menyenangkan, serta setelah kembali dari liburan memiliki produktivitas kerja yang lebih baik," ujar Warsito.

Lebih lanjut, Warsito menyampaikan bahwa keberhasilan penyelenggaraan Nataru memerlukan pembagian peran dan sinergi antarkementerian/lembaga sesuai dengan tugas dan kewenangan masing-masing. Untuk itu, rapat koordinasi dilakukan secara berjenjang dan menjadi konsolidasi lintas sektor serta bahan pelaksanaan Rapat Koordinasi Tingkat Menteri.

Warsito selanjutnya menggarisbawahi empat aspek utama yang perlu menjadi perhatian bersama dalam penyelenggaraan pelayanan Nataru, yaitu kelancaran, kenyamanan, keselamatan, dan keamanan masyarakat.

Dari aspek kelancaran, Warsito mendorong peninjauan potensi Flexible Work Arrangement (FWA), serta mendukung pengaturan lalu lintas dan penyeberangan melalui SKB Kementerian Perhubungan, Kementerian Pekerjaan Umum, dan Kepolisian. Ketersediaan BBM serta stimulus ekonomi berupa diskon tarif transportasi juga perlu dioptimalkan. Sementara dari aspek kenyamanan, kesiapan sarana dan prasarana tempat ibadah, materi khotbah Natal yang menyejukkan, serta fasilitas pariwisata dan rest area perlu dipastikan.

Pada aspek keselamatan dan keamanan, Warsito mengingatkan pentingnya kesiapan fasilitas kesehatan baik di pusat peribadatan maupun jalur mudik, termasuk kelayakan armada transportasi, sekaligus kewaspadaan terhadap risiko cuaca dan bencana. Penguatan pengamanan melalui Operasi Lilin dan posko terpadu juga menjadi sektor yang perlu dikoordinasikan.

Dalam rapat tersebut, seluruh kementerian/lembaga dan BUMN memaparkan berbagai kesiapan dukungan Nataru, meliputi kesiapan ibadah Natal, penyiapan kebijakan FWA, serta kesiapan transportasi darat, udara, dan penyeberangan, termasuk pengoperasian jalur tol fungsional, rute alternatif, rest area, dan stimulus tarif. Selain itu, disampaikan pula kesiapan SDM dan sarana tanggap bencana, fasilitas dan layanan kesehatan, posko terpadu, serta dukungan logistik dan pengamanan untuk menjamin kelancaran distribusi kebutuhan pokok selama periode Nataru.

Sebagai informasi, dalam rangka mendukung mobilitas masyarakat selama Nataru 2026/2027, pemerintah juga memberikan stimulus diskon tarif transportasi meliputi diskon 30% tiket kereta api, diskon 30% tarif dasar kapal laut, pembebasan 100% jasa kepelabuhanan penyeberangan, serta insentif PPN Ditanggung Pemerintah (DTP) untuk transportasi udara. Kebijakan ini diharapkan meningkatkan aksesibilitas perjalanan, konektivitas antarwilayah, dan daya beli masyarakat.

Menutup rapat, Warsito mengajak seluruh kementerian/lembaga untuk memperkuat komitmen dan sinergi dalam memastikan kesiapan pelayanan Nataru secara menyeluruh. Seluruh aspek persiapan perlu dikawal sejak dini melalui koordinasi yang berkesinambungan agar berbagai kebutuhan dan potensi permasalahan dapat diantisipasi sebelum periode libur berlangsung.

"Kita juga perlu memastikan distribusi bahan pokok telah menjangkau daerah tujuan sebelum pemberlakuan pembatasan kendaraan sumbu tiga. Jangan sampai pengaturan lalu lintas justru menghambat pasokan kebutuhan masyarakat. Karena itu, seluruh potensi kendala harus diantisipasi sejak dini," pungkas Warsito.

Turut hadir dalam rapat tersebut antara lain perwakilan dari Kementerian Agama, Kementerian Dalam Negeri; Kementerian PANRB, Kementerian Ketenagakerjaan, Kementerian Perhubungan, Kementerian Kesehatan, Kementerian Pekerjaan Umum, Kepolisian Negara RI, Tentara Nasional Indonesia, BNPB, BMKG, BASARNAS, Jasa Marga, dan ASDP.

Jakarta – Direktur Jenderal Potensi Pertahanan Kementerian Pertahanan Republik Indonesia (Dirjen Pothan Kemhan RI) Laksda TNI Sri Yanto, S.T., secara resmi menutup Pertemuan ke-12 Defence Industry Cooperation Committee (DICC) Republik Indonesia–Republik Korea di Aula Bela Negara, Kementerian Pertahanan RI, Jakarta, Rabu (11/11/2026).

Dalam pertemuan tersebut, Dirjen Pothan Kemhan RI memimpin delegasi Indonesia mewakili Sekretaris Jenderal Kemhan RI, sedangkan delegasi Republik Korea dipimpin oleh Deputy Minister of Advanced Capabilities Program, Defense Acquisition Program Administration (DAPA), Jeoung Giyoung.

Pertemuan DICC ke-12 dilaksanakan untuk meninjau pelaksanaan hasil DICC ke-11, menyelesaikan berbagai hal yang masih tertunda, serta menetapkan langkah-langkah tindak lanjut kerja sama kedua negara. Pertemuan mengusung tema “Penguatan Kerja Sama Industri Pertahanan Indonesia–Korea Selatan melalui Teknologi, Kemitraan Industri, dan Kolaborasi Berkelanjutan”.

Dalam sambutan penutupan, Dirjen Pothan Kemhan RI menyampaikan apresiasi kepada delegasi Republik Korea, instansi pemerintah, serta pelaku industri pertahanan kedua negara atas kontribusi dan komitmen yang diberikan selama pelaksanaan pertemuan. “Kemitraan yang kita bangun harus meningkatkan kemampuan Industri Pertahanan kedua negara,” Ujar Dirjen Pothan Kemhan.

Sementara itu, Deputy Minister of Advanced Capabilities Program DAPA menyampaikan penghargaan dan terima kasih kepada seluruh anggota delegasi kedua negara yang telah berkontribusi dalam membangun diskusi yang terbuka, tulus, dan konstruktif sepanjang pelaksanaan pertemuan.

Rangkaian kegiatan dilanjutkan dengan penandatanganan Minutes of Meeting (MoM) oleh kedua ketua delegasi sebagai dasar tindak lanjut atas hasil pembahasan antarpemerintah dan antarpelaku industri. Selain itu, dilaksanakan penandatanganan sejumlah nota kesepahaman (Memorandum of Understanding/MoU) business-to-business (B2B) yang mencakup kerja sama di sektor dirgantara dan amunisi.

Pada kesempatan yang sama, dilaksanakan juga penyerahan secara simbolis satu unit bus listrik dan dua unit kendaraan SUV dari Hyundai Indonesia kepada Kementerian Pertahanan RI.

Rangkaian Pertemuan DICC ke-12 kemudian diakhiri dengan jamuan makan malam bersama di Hotel AYANA, Jakarta. Jamuan tersebut menjadi momentum bagi para pelaku industri pertahanan Indonesia dan Republik Korea untuk mempererat hubungan secara langsung (people-to-people contacts) dan melanjutkan komunikasi yang telah terjalin selama pertemuan. While Claude Motion excels in speed and scalability, human editors bring irreplaceable qualities to video production. That said, findings suggest AI tools like Claude can manage 80% of the heavy lifting in video editing, leaving the final 20% for human input. This division allows editors to focus on refining details and adding emotional depth.

Claude Motion is ideal for creators aiming to produce high-quality social media content quickly and affordably. Its user-friendly design makes it accessible even to those with no prior editing experience. By following the outlined workflow and using custom Claude Motion skills, users can create motion reels in as little as 20 minutes.

For professional editors, Claude offers a way to accelerate workflows and scale production without compromising quality. However, projects requiring high levels of creativity and emotional nuance may still benefit from human expertise.

Claude Motion’s ability to deliver polished videos at a fraction of the time and cost of traditional methods positions it as a valuable tool for modern content creation.
